Tenant scoping covers the primary row, not the ids that point to related rows. `POST /api/activities` with a `leadId` copied from another organization creates an activity in your org attached to their lead (`activityService.ts:64-67`; the schema only requires that the lead exists, `schema.prisma:461`). The same gap exists for `companyId`, `sourceLeadId` and `primaryContactId` on leads, contacts and deals (see `docs/architecture/README.md` finding A2). The unused `assertSameTenant()` (`tenantContext.ts:31-36`) is the intended fix.

items.front: 5: The UI treats every bootstrap error as "please log in".
items.back: `WorkspaceShell` renders `DemoLoginCard` whenever `useWorkspace()` errors (`src/components/layout/workspace-shell.tsx:32-38`). A 403 `organization_unavailable` or a 500 looks identical to a logged-out state, which makes support tickets hard to triage.

items.label: f04-unlogged-500
items.front: What does route() do with an unexpected error, and what is missing?
items.back: Returns 500 { error: { code: 'internal_server_error' } }. The original error is not logged anywhere in the function, and requestId is never written to a log or AuditLog, so a 500 leaves almost no server-side trace.
(`authService.ts:14-73`). See section 1. A production build needs real credentials or an explicit `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "production") throw` on this route.

items.front: 3: Invitation tokens are readable by managers.
items.back: `GET /api/org/invitations` requires only `org.users.read` (`src/app/api/org/invitations/route.ts:20`), which `SALES_MANAGER` holds (`policy.ts:42`). It returns full `Invitation` rows (`invitationRepository.ts:16-21`) including `token` (`schema.prisma:258`). No accept-invitation route exists yet, so the token is not currently exploitable, but the first person to add one inherits the leak.

items.label: f01-four-review-points
items.front: Four points to score when reviewing the deal-stage null guard
items.back: Uses the shared error contract (notFoundError, deal_not_found); sits directly after the repository result; failure skips history and audit; the success path is unchanged. Also: the message must not claim a specific database race was observed.

items.label: f03-claims-not-read
items.front: Where does the tenant come from: the JWT's activeOrganizationId claim or the database?
items.back: The database. activeOrganizationId is written into the token but never read back; getOptionalSession extracts only sub and activeMembershipId, and the tenant is derived from the reloaded membership.

items.label: f02-tenant-guard-order
items.front: The four checks requireOrgRequest runs, in order
items.back: 1) tenantId and membership present (403 tenant_scope_required); 2) membership ACTIVE (403 inactive_membership); 3) org ACTIVE or TRIALING (403 organization_unavailable); 4) role holds the permission, if one was passed (403 permission_denied).
